newsitem.title: INDIA: India panel for removal of OTCEI listing limit.
newsitem.headline: India panel for removal of OTCEI listing limit.

text.p: The Over The Counter Exchange of India (OTCEI) must allow all companies to list on its bourse, a committee said on Friday.
At present, only companies with a paid-up capital of less than 50 million rupees are allowed to list on the OTCEI.
The committee was appointed in April by market regulator Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) to suggest ways to revamp the working of OTCEI.
"Investors in all companies which have a post-issue equity of less than 100 million rupees should have the benefit of market making and sponsorship," the committee said.
"If these (recommendations) are done, then OTCEI should pick up fairly fast," committee chairman S.A Dave told reporters.
The measure was among a number of recommendations made by the committee to revitalise the OTCEI.
OTCEI, India's first exchange to introduce electronic trade and market making, was started in 1990 to assist promoters of small companies and help retail investors.
The OTCEI's network of dealers and members is spread over 42 cities in India.

The exchange failed to take off as the lack of adequate funding from financial institutions and settlement problems affected operations. It has been dogged by inadequate trading volumes and poor interest shown by small promoters and dealers.

"A small corpus of about 500 million to one billion rupees by promoter institutions for investment in fundamentally strong OTCEI listed stocks would certainly provide a considerable boost to the OTCEI market," the committee said.

The OTCEI was promoted by state-run institutions like the Unit Trust of India, the Life Insurance Corp, Industrial Development Bank of India and Industrial Credit and Investment Corp of India among others.
